name: marble-drop
title: Marble drop: a physics toy with pegs, gravity and tilt
summary: Thirty glowing marbles fall under gravity through a staggered field of pegs, bounce off them and the side walls and drop into bins whose floor flashes in the marble's colour. Tap anywhere to drop a marble right there; tilt the device and gravity follows the accelerometer. The physics is real: velocity, gravity, restitution, peg collisions with push-out, four sub-steps per frame, all integrated by the player in particle equations.
prompt: A physics toy: colourful balls falling under gravity and bouncing off pegs and walls, tap to drop a new ball where I tap, tilt the phone to change gravity. Make it satisfying.
hand_built: A physics simulation is the lesson: the state and the integrator are a particle system written by hand, and nothing in the component library simulates.
teaches: A particle system is a physics engine: each marble's state (x, y, vx, vy and helpers) is a particle variable, and the particlesLoop equations are one explicit-Euler step that the player runs for every marble on every frame
Sub-steps: four particlesLoop ops over the same system, each with dt = min(deltaTime(), 0.04) / 4, integrate four times per frame. Collisions stay tight because a marble moves about 1 px per step

Equations update simultaneously from the previous step's values, so a helper variable lags one step. The peg offsets fu, fw are computed from the position predicted 4 steps ahead (x + y + (vx + vy) * 4 * dt) so they line up with the position the collision impulse acts on

The nearest peg of a staggered lattice in two roundings: pegs sit where u = x + y and w = x − y are multiples of S, so fu = u − round(u / S) * S, fw = w − round(w / S) * S, the offset is ((fu + fw) / 2, (fu − fw) / 2) and the squared distance is (fu² + fw²) / 2

Collision response is an impulse J = (1 + e) / (4R²) * min(v · offset, 0), applied once (J resets on the step after it fires) plus a push-out P that removes the overlap; walls reflect vx with a guarded factor wl

Tap to drop: onTouchDown records @tx, @ty and counts @drops; each marble compares @drops with the count it last saw, and the one whose index equals @slot respawns at the touch. Fifteen marbles auto-rain from the top, fifteen are reserved for taps
Tilt: gravity is (−accelerationX(), accelerationY()) scaled to the screen, falling back to straight down when the sensor reads under 2 m/s² (no sensor, or the device lying flat)

Colour per marble without colour expressions: five particlesComparison passes over index ranges [0, 6), [6, 12)… each paint the marbles of one colour; the peg they last hit flashes as a fading ring in that colour
pitfalls: There are no marble-to-marble collisions. The format can express them (ParticlesCompare with two equation sets compares every pair, reading particle1/particle2 values through the CMD1/CMD2 tokens), but json2rc has no infix syntax for those tokens, so pairwise equations cannot be written in JSON today. Marbles pass through each other: visible when a tilt piles them against a wall
Every equation must fit in 32 RPN entries (Android): split long formulas into helper variables, and remember each helper adds a step of lag
createParticles initialValues are evaluated without the document's variables in the C++ player: use literals and the index u only; put spawns in the equations
ifElse is ifElse(else, then, cond): getting it backwards froze the exit timer and no marble ever spawned
rand() in the equations makes runs differ per player and per seed: compare players by behaviour, not pixels (render with seed for a repeatable image)
rc-inspect's audit reports dt as dead_code: it does not count reads from particle equations

check.describe: A dark indigo board titled 'Marble drop' / 'Tap to drop a marble · tilt to tip', a staggered field of pale pegs and seven bins at the bottom. After a few seconds pink, amber, green, blue and violet marbles with soft halos are spread through the pegs, each with a fading ring on the peg it last hit, and a bin floor glows where one has just landed. Taps: five new marbles appear where tapped (120, 200 and 150 px down). Tilted (accelerationX −6, Y 7.5): the marbles slide right and pile along the right wall.
